summary: This resolution sets procedures for House floor consideration of eight bills on D.C. criminal justice changes, FERC interconnection reforms, reestablishing the National Coal Council, and border-crossing facility approvals by waiving points of order, deeming substitute amendments adopted, limiting each to one hour of debate, and allowing one motion to recommit.

scores.thoughts: The resolution is a procedural rules package and contains no provisions that authorize, appropriate, or alter any federal spending levels.
No tax provisions, rate changes, or revenue measures appear in the text.
The resolution does not address healthcare policy, coverage, or regulation.
No references to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The border-crossing facilities bill (H.R. 3062) concerns energy infrastructure, not immigration or border security for persons.
No provisions related to reproductive rights or abortion access.
No military, defense, or national security spending or policy changes are involved.

Sections 5 and 6 facilitate consideration of H.R. 3015 (reestablishing the National Coal Council) and H.R. 3062 (streamlining approvals for oil, gas, and electricity border facilities). These bills advance fossil-fuel infrastructure and industry advisory structures, which align with limiting environmental regulations.
No welfare, entitlement, or social-services provisions are present.
The resolution does not address schools, funding, or education policy.
No drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related measures are referenced.

Sections 2(a)–(d) bring forward H.R. 4922, 5143, 5140, and 5125, which tighten youth-offender definitions, expand police pursuit authority, lower the age for adult trials, and alter D.C. sentencing and judicial processes. These measures advance tougher sentencing and policing approaches.
No trade agreements, tariffs, or globalization provisions are included.
The resolution contains no fiscal, deficit, or debt-related language.
No provisions concerning LGBTQ legal protections or rights.
No foreign-aid authorizations or reductions are addressed.
No election administration, voting access, or integrity measures appear.
Section 7 incorporates CBDC restrictions into another bill, but this is a narrow, technical addition with minimal overall bearing on tech regulation or privacy policy.
No labor, union, or workplace provisions are present.
No religious-liberty or anti-discrimination provisions are included.
